events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.70)
events.body:
The trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3] and that the driver's traffic excuse fails: the only speed-band record on the replaced stretch is PIE band 2 [F12], but the trace marks no qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch, and a band alone does not exempt under RD-4(b) [F15][RD-4]. So the segment can only be excused by the rider's prior agreement.

That agreement is real and prior: at 22:35 the driver proposed "go round via Bukit Timah Road" [F8] and at 22:36 the rider answered "Can lah, go ahead" [F9], both messages timestamped [F10], i.e. before the segment's 22:39 start, satisfying the "before you go" timing of RD-5 [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement repeating the same [F11] adds nothing and is not itself consent (G11). But the agreed words name a specific road — "via Bukit Timah Road" — so under RD-5 this is a specific named-road authorisation that covers driving on Bukit Timah Road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road [F8][F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the fact table names the road driven during 22:39–22:50 [F3][F10]; the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3]. Timing alone does not tie them (G13). The rider raised exactly this doubt ("Was that even the road he said?") and the trace's RD-5 and RD-3 branches are both left "?" [F8][F9][F11].

This is a rider-named-place question with no stop measured in the segment, so RD-3(a) cannot apply: no rider message named a specific place where the car stopped [F8][F9][F10][RD-3]. The segment is therefore neither tied to the agreed road nor placed somewhere else, and the finding is undetermined rather than exempt or counting [F3][RD-5]. Because that finding changes the amount, the case must go to a person (G13).

The money at stake is definite if the segment is not excused: 7.34 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.77 km adds 4.57 km [F3]; at this trip's own rate, distance fare $34.35 ÷ 24.36 km = $1.4101/km [F7], the refund would be 4.57 × $1.4101 = $6.44, i.e. 6.44 SGD, refund_partial. The billed excess already on the meter is $6.66 (4.72 km × $1.4101/km) [F4], and waiting is meter time 0.4 min × $0.26 = $0.11 [F5], which under RD-3(c) is not refundable for a metered taxi [RD-3]. Because the record cannot settle the segment, I do not execute that amount here and escalate instead.

Nothing in the chat, the statement or the complaint contains any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation: the exchange is a route negotiation [F8][F9][F11], so the SAFE screen is none [SAFE-1]. No driver-side aggravating flag arises: the profile shows zero upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6 is not met [F18][RD-6].
